newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Anderton says discussing issues paper with Labour.
newsitem.headline: Anderton says discussing issues paper with Labour.

text.p: Alliance Party leader Jim Anderton said on Wednesday his party would discuss the Alliance issues paper when it meet with the Labour Party this evening.

The two parties would also discuss how issues of confidence would be handled should New Zealand First side with Labour to form a coalition government. Such a government would need the support of the Alliance to gain a majority.
Anderton told reporters the parties would discuss what conditions of confidence Labour and New Zealand First would require from the Alliance and what the requirements were for the Alliance to meet.
Anderton said: "Sooner or later we have to see the nature of the programme in order to agree with it."
Asked what the purpose of the talks were, he said: to form an alternative government to the present National one.

Labour and New Zealand First jointly hold 54 seats in the 120-seat parliament against 53 for National, Act and United. The Alliance has said it would remain outside a coalition, but could give support on certain matters.
The Alliance has presented a policy paper to Labour, covering issues such as health, education, superannuation, the environment and foreign investment.
